questions.question: A REST Dispatch Class in IRIS must extend which base class?
questions.explanation: REST Dispatch Classes in IRIS extend %CSP.REST. This base class provides the routing engine, %request/%response objects, and CORS support.

questions.question: In a REST ClassMethod, how do you set the HTTP response status to 404 Not Found?
questions.explanation: HTTP status is set via SET %response.Status = "404 Not Found". The return value of the ClassMethod ($$$OK) signals ObjectScript execution status — not the HTTP status code.

questions.question: What does the following REST ClassMethod return to the client?

options.text: The raw %Status value as a string
The person object serialized as JSON, or a 404 response if not found
Nothing — RETURN $$$OK stops execution before JSON is written

questions.explanation: %JSONExport() writes the JSON representation of the object to the output stream (sent as the HTTP response body). If %OpenId returns "", the 404 status is set and the method exits early.

questions.question: Where are REST routes defined in a manual-coding Dispatch Class?

options.text: In an XData block named UrlMap with <Routes> XML
In a JSON file referenced by the class

questions.explanation: Routes are declared in an XData UrlMap block with XML <Routes> and <Route> elements specifying Url, Method, and Call.

questions.question: How do you read the JSON body of an incoming POST request inside a REST ClassMethod?
questions.explanation: The request body is available via %request.Content (a stream). {}.%FromJSON(%request.Content) parses it into a dynamic object.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about %JSON.Adaptor? (select all that apply)

options.text: A class that extends %JSON.Adaptor gains %JSONExport() and %JSONImport() methods
%JSONExport() writes the serialized JSON directly to the current output device (stdout)
%JSON.Adaptor can only be mixed into %Persistent classes
The JSONNAME property parameter overrides the JSON field name during serialization
%JSONImport() both deserializes JSON and automatically calls %Save()

questions.explanation: A: Correct. B: Correct — %JSONExport() writes to stdout (the HTTP response). C: Wrong — %JSON.Adaptor can be mixed into any class (%Persistent, %Registered, etc.). D: Correct — JSONNAME renames the field in JSON output. E: Wrong — %JSONImport() only deserializes; you must call %Save() separately.

questions.question: What must be configured in the IRIS Management Portal before a Dispatch Class can receive HTTP requests?

options.text: A Web Application entry with the correct URL path prefix and Dispatch Class
An SSL certificate even for internal (non-HTTPS) endpoints

questions.explanation: A Web Application must be created in Management Portal → Security → Web Applications, specifying the URL path prefix and the Dispatch Class. Without it, IRIS has no way to route HTTP requests to your class.

questions.question: In the specification-first REST approach, after importing an OpenAPI spec into IRIS:

options.text: IRIS generates only an Implementation Class; you must write the Dispatch Class manually
IRIS generates both a Dispatch Class (routing, do not edit) and an Implementation Class (write your logic here)
IRIS generates a single class that contains both routing and business logic
The spec is stored but no code is generated until you manually trigger compilation

questions.explanation: Specification-first generates two classes: a Dispatch Class that handles routing (auto-managed, should not be edited) and an Implementation Class with stub methods where you write business logic.

questions.question: What does the following code print?
questions.code:
SET obj = {}
SET obj.name = "Alice"
SET obj.age = 30
WRITE obj.%ToJSON(), !

options.text: Error — dynamic objects cannot mix string and numeric values

questions.explanation: IRIS dynamic objects ({}) serialize to standard JSON via %ToJSON(). The output is {"name":"Alice","age":30}. Mixing string and numeric values is fully valid.

questions.question: In a REST UrlMap, a route is defined as <Route Url="/orders/:id" Method="GET" Call="GetOrder"/>. Which method signature correctly handles this route?
questions.explanation: URL path parameters (:id) are passed as positional arguments to the ClassMethod. The parameter name must match the placeholder name in the Url pattern.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about CORS in IRIS REST are correct? (select all that apply)

options.text: CORS is enabled by default for all REST endpoints
CORS must be explicitly enabled in the Web Application settings in the Management Portal
Without CORS enabled, browsers will block cross-origin requests to the IRIS REST API
CORS configuration is done inside the Dispatch Class using a Parameter

questions.explanation: B: Correct — CORS is off by default and must be explicitly enabled in Web Application settings. C: Correct — browsers enforce CORS and will block requests if the server does not send the correct headers. A is wrong (CORS is not on by default). D is wrong (CORS is not configured in the Dispatch Class).

questions.question: What is the correct return value at the end of every REST ClassMethod, regardless of the HTTP status code sent?
questions.explanation: REST ClassMethods always RETURN $$$OK at the end. This signals to the IRIS CSP engine that ObjectScript execution completed without a fatal error. The actual HTTP status code is controlled separately via %response.Status.
